solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: When speaking, leaves puddings

indicators.note: the clue asks for the word as it is spoken, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: to leave someone is to desert them, so leaves gives deserts

explanation.surface: Someone, while talking, abandons the sweet course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Desserts are the sweet courses served after the main meal, commonly called puddings in Britain.

clue.text: Detective Inspector had led corrupt swindle

parts.note: DI is the standard abbreviation for a Detective Inspector in British police
had shortens to 'd, as in I'd, giving D

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or twisted out of shape, so the letters of led are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior police officer led a crooked operation to cheat people.
explanation.definitionFit: To diddle is informal British slang meaning to cheat or con someone out of money.

clue.text: Stage in endlessly severe horse race

indicators.note: the stage word is placed in the middle of the shortened severe word
endlessly means the last letter of the word for severe is cut off

parts.note: severe means stern
a leg is a stage of a journey or contest

explanation.surface: A phase within a harsh, gruelling horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' looks like the definition of a theatre but is the LEG of a journey; 'endlessly' leaves STER, and 'in' places the stage there.
explanation.definitionFit: The St Leger is a classic flat race run at Doncaster, the oldest of England's five Classics.

clue.text: Young fish always crossing lake

indicators.note: the word for always spans or straddles the lake letter, so it holds it inside

parts.note: always means ever
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A juvenile fish keeps swimming across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a fish at an early stage of growth migrating upriver.

clue.text: Sailor's dark waterproof coat

definitions.meaning: ..., short for tarpaulin, is old slang for a sailor
the black sticky substance used as a waterproof coating

explanation.surface: A seaman owns a black oilskin jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is slang for a seaman, and tar coats ropes and hulls against water.

clue.text: Vagrant finally failing to find public transport

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for vagrant fails, meaning it drops away

parts.note: a vagrant is a tramp

explanation.surface: A homeless wanderer ends up unable to locate a bus or train.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a street vehicle running on rails, a form of mass transit in many cities.

clue.text: At first, rent handled in old money

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Initially the rent was paid in pre-decimal coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old British slang for cash, recorded since the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Drastically alter letter from Greek gallery

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
the Tate is the famous group of London art galleries

explanation.surface: Radically change a message sent from a Greek art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to undergo or cause a fundamental change of form.

clue.text: Again correct poor Dieter

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in bad shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fix the work of a weak man named Dieter once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit is to revise text a second time, making further corrections.

clue.text: Transport ruminants, about 54

indicators.note: the ruminants go about, that is around, the number in Roman numerals

parts.note: deer are cud-chewing animals, ruminants
fifty-four in Roman numerals is LIV

explanation.surface: Move some cud-chewing animals, around fifty-four of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver is to carry goods to a destination, a verb sense of transport.

clue.text: Poet and old priest to back

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

indicators.note: back tells us the word to is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: A writer of verse and an elderly cleric return.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was the modernist author of The Waste Land, a famous writer of verse.

clue.text: Beer barrel a German holds

indicators.note: the words barrel a German hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A cask of ale is kept by a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light, bottom-fermented style of ale, originally from Germany.

clue.text: Bog plant Rod tore in a frenzy

indicators.note: a frenzy is wild agitation, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Rod wildly ripped up a marsh plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Redroot is a North American marsh herb, the bloodwort, growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Right to declare one's a partygoer

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert

explanation.surface: Someone has the entitlement to announce that they are a clubber.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver is someone who goes to wild parties or all-night dance events.

clue.text: Go off with a tank and yellow digger

parts.note: food that goes off rots
a vat is a large tank for liquids
or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: Something goes bad alongside a yellow vehicle on a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotavator is a motorised machine with rotating blades for breaking up soil.

clue.text: On reflection it failed to get straightened

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so the word it is read backwards

parts.note: something that failed, like an engine, died

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, the project collapsed before it could be set right.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidied means put in order, made neat, much as straightened a room.

clue.text: Entertains Rex, say, with beers

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king, as in royal cyphers
say means for example, abbreviated EG
ales are beers

explanation.surface: Someone named Rex, perhaps, hosts friends with plenty of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale is to delight or amuse company, often with stories or food and drink.

clue.text: I'm pursuing figure immediately

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this word follows the figure

parts.note: a stat, short for statistic, is a figure
I'm without its apostrophe gives the letters

explanation.surface: I am chasing a number straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Stat or statim is Latin used by doctors and nurses for at once, without delay.

clue.text: Good length bindweed regularly and effortless moved

definitions.note: the clue prints effortless where effortlessly is meant, an adverb with the verb

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of bindweed

explanation.surface: A long, healthy creeper spread steadily and easily across a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of bindweed: IDED.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide is to travel smoothly and without apparent effort, as a skater or bird does.

clue.text: Closed group, as requested

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
an order is a group, as of monks or knights

explanation.surface: A private society, just as was asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: Made to order means produced according to a customer's specific instructions.

clue.text: Willow tree somehow rose around one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the numeral for one
somehow implies some unexplained change, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A willow somehow grew up beside a single plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a species of willow whose flexible shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Note lass is like a Queen!

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a gal is a girl or lass

explanation.surface: Observe that a young woman is very much a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means royal or befitting a monarch, as a queen would be.

clue.text: Regret penning English verse for show

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the regret word goes around the others

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry for writing English poetry for a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical entertainment of sketches, songs and dances.

clue.text: Labour candidate finally producing fine material

parts.note: toil means hard labour

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word candidate

explanation.surface: A Labour Party candidate ends up making delicate cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party but is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Toile is a fine linen or cotton cloth, often printed with pastoral scenes.

clue.text: Hated vicar I escorted

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar
to escort someone is to lead them, past tense led

explanation.surface: Someone loathed the parish priest whom the speaker accompanied.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviled means abused or denounced with contempt, close to despised.

clue.text: Snitch irate to be missing tips

indicators.note: losing its tips means the word irate loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An informer becomes furious when not given any gratuities.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat is to inform on someone, telling tales to the authorities.

clue.text: Dull hosts run trading centre

indicators.note: hosts means takes in as a guest, so the dull word holds the run letter

parts.note: mat, or matt, describes a dull non-glossy finish
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A boring host lays on a race at a marketplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A mart is a market, a place where goods are bought and sold.

clue.text: Emphasised fantastic des res on street

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the street abbreviation comes first and the jumble follows
fantastic means wildly fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An estate agent highlighted a wonderful desirable residence on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'des res' is estate-agent shorthand for a desirable residence; 'fantastic' scrambles it into RESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed means accented or given emphasis, as a syllable or point is.
